name: The Valley of the Iron Shroud (station 4, Trap F1; PLAN.md sections 4.2 and 6): Wadi al-Kafan, a dead-end glacial box-canyon 6 km long cut into the fault blocks north-west of Open Sprint 1 at 4,720 m (0.88 atm): a wide gentle mouth with a lukewarm iron seep that promises an oasis, 600 m walls of columned titanium basalt, a 35 m reverse moraine lip 4 km in, behind it the sealed katabatic cold sink (-8 C by day, -34 C at night) on blue ice littered with the rimed wreckage of betrayed caravans, the hanging glacier's seracs over the headwall, and the Guide's Needle, the iron-runged chimney up the east wall by which the guide leaves
